reviewer: Codex session, review explicitly requested by the user
scope: Every positive Sonnet finding in the three specified rubrics, across all three libraries

assessment_meaning.useful_candidate: Specific useful improvement supported by source inspection; exact replacement uncompiled
assessment_meaning.optional_refactor: Plausible suggestion, but benefit or claimed defect not compelling
assessment_meaning.not_established: The finding does not establish the claimed defect
assessment_meaning.outside_rubric: The proposed improvement belongs to another audit
assessment_meaning.incorrect_or_incomplete_proposal: The proposed abstraction does not cover its cited uses as stated

missing-structure.reason: There are genuine bundling opportunities, but the rubric admits generic implementation reuse, already-available structure and hypothetical consumers.
missing-structure.proposed_rubric: Find a map or mathematical object whose useful algebraic, topological or inverse structure is exposed only as separate facts. Identify the standard bundle, explain how its fields are supplied, and show an actual consumer that benefits. Do not count structure already available through an existing public object, implementation via a generic combinator, or unused hypothetical API. Preserve useful names and account for the cost of bundling.

fragile-proofs.recommendation: drop as a separate judge-only quality score for now
fragile-proofs.reason: Most findings infer fragility from ordinary simp, rfl, case analysis, coercions or potential API changes. Some concrete improvements are useful, but overlap proof simplification and do not validate a reliable source-only fragility measure.
fragile-proofs.alternative: Route specific simplifications to the readability audit. A future robustness experiment should define a controlled semantics-preserving perturbation, reproduce a failure, and check that the proposed repair survives it.

repeated-proof-machinery.reason: Substantial common arguments are visible in multiple libraries, especially cutoff integrals, Gaussian bounds, shell geometry and tensor combinatorics. Short proof patterns and speculative universal helpers should not receive the same finding.
repeated-proof-machinery.proposed_rubric: Find a substantial mathematical argument repeated at two or more source locations. Give a precise shared lemma, or an existing lemma to reuse, and explain how it applies at every cited location under the actual assumptions and import dependencies. Show a net improvement including the helper statement/proof and all call sites. Common tactics, routine inductions, short case splits and moving repetition into a more complicated abstraction are insufficient.
